Andy Urbach
Explore FirstLight 102mm Doublet Refractor Telescope with Twilight Nano Mount

I bought this to use with a Svbony SV550 80mm, since there isn't a focal reducer designed specifically for this telescope. Because all the specifications are practically the same as the Explore Scientific ED80 Essential Series Triplet Refractor, I decided to give it a try. The performance is excellent, considering the corrector wasn't made for the SV550. There was significant aberration, but only near the edges of an APS-C sensor. I recommend it, but keep in mind that it only corrects about 90% of the APS-C sensor on the SV550 telescope. It may perform even better to the ED80 telescope.

Gabriel M
0.8x Focal Reducer

Love it! I can see the craters of the moon in great detail. I'm hoping the weather where I'm at clears up so I can try to view planets next!

Christina Yonts
Explore FirstLight 100mm Mak-Cassegrain Telescope with EQ3 Mount

This thing is INCREDIBLE for the price. I paid $99 for the 114mm + Twilight Nano Mount. The OTA and mount feel really sturdy and well-made. The red-dot feels flimsy but performs well. I highly recommend collimating the scope when you receive it. My first views of Jupiter were very poor until I collimated the scope. With the standard 25mm Plössl and proper collimation, Jupiter’s rings were easily visible at just 20x. I highly recommend investing in GOOD eyepieces too for easier viewing. Overall, I’d highly recommend to someone looking for a high-quality budget telescope. The images in my review were taken through the basic 25mm eyepiece and a 5mm Celestron X-Cel LX eyepiece by my phone.

Miller L.
Explore FirstLight 114mm Newtonian Telescope with Twilight Nano Mount

Great value scope, especially with everything that comes with it (2-speed focuser, finderscope, diagonal, cradle/mount plate). Very solidly built, feels high-quality. Focuser is smooth. I've had it for nearly two years now and taken it to several astronomy club events and it's held up without issue, and it's easy to transport. Views are clear and sharp. Whether pointing it at the moon, Saturn, or the Andromeda Galaxy, it's gotten plenty of "ooohs" and "aaahs" from people at star parties.

Now, this scope was also my intro to tracked astrophotography. Being a doublet, I knew it would have limitations, but for the price it still delivers pleasing (to a beginner at least) imaging capabilities if you're willing to take the time to work with it. It is also heavy, which is a factor for what mounts can handle it. I may have gotten lucky, but the IExos-100 with the basic tripod and no AZ adjuster has been solid with this scope and once I figured out guiding I'm frequently within 0.3 - 0.5. I keep the tripod legs fully retracted and try to be meticulous with balancing, but it works. I was even able to rig the included finder scope to accept a guide camera, so made the setup even more cost-effective. There's obviously some star bloat/halos, sometimes a LOT, but my skill and processing abilities are a bigger limiting factor at the moment than the scope. I definitely want to upgrade at some point, especially for something with a wider FOV, but I don't feel like it's a necessity at this point to continue growing in this hobby.

Ryan W

Richard VICKERY
8x50 Illuminated Right Angle Polar Finder Scope with NEW long battery life Illuminator II

The iEXOS-100-2 PMC-Eight may not be considered by some to be an all around "premium" mount, but if you are looking for an inexpensive German Equatorial Mount as a starting point this one might be just what the Doctor ordered. I have three other mounts from different brands that are controlled by ASI Air Plus controllers and I use them for DSO astrophotography. The PCM Eight mount was chosen because I was building a dedicated Solar Imaging rig with a Lunt Solar systems LS50T Ha (Hydrogen Alpha) telescope. I didn't need a mount that could carry a massive payload, I wasn't going to need the typical accessories (EFW, EAF, Dew Heaters, etc.) and I really didn't want to spend a ton of money. My first test run with an ASI Air Mini was less then satisfactory so I switched to MeLee Quieter 3Q mini-PC running Windows 11 and ASCOM/NINA. Unfortunately this configuration didn't perform any better, so I wiped the mini-PC and installed Stellarmate OS. The difference was like night and day. Up until this point I was a die hard Air user and I have never really been keen on using anything that required desktop sharing, but for some strange reason neither of those systems seemed to like the PMC-Eight. There were disconnects, random tracking turn-offs, and difficulties with Park and Home functionality. The first time the PC booted into Stellarmate the mount connected on the first shot and it never skipped a beat. The Stellarmate UI is different from the Air and NINA UIs, but once you get a a handle on it everything falls into place.
